quarterly_data.signal: CFO Guy Kizner on Q1 2026 GAAP detail: gross margin 57.7% GAAP; operating margin 30% GAAP; GAAP EPS $2.04 per diluted share; operating expenses $64.9 million GAAP and $59.4 million non-GAAP; effective tax rate approximately 17%, 'modestly above our guidance', expected to normalize as the year progresses. Q2 2026 guidance beyond revenue: GAAP EPS $2.10-$2.24; at the midpoint gross margin approximately 57% GAAP and approximately 59% non-GAAP ('Usually when we are guiding it's at ±1%'), GAAP operating expenses approximately $72 million and non-GAAP approximately $66 million, non-GAAP financial income approximately $16 million, effective tax rate approximately 15%. For full-year 2026 the CFO sees gross margins 'within the same rate that we're giving the guidance for the first half of the year' and 'sustainable during the year' (target model 57%-60%).

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Gaby Waisman on demand and supply: 'AI investments remain the fundamental driver of industry growth, with a shift towards agentic AI models increasing computing and memory requirements', accelerating capacity expansion across logic, memory and advanced packaging and driving higher process control and metrology intensity. She expects memory 'to become more dominant this year compared to last one on the backdrop of investments in advanced DRAM'. Logic: 'We are seeing growing investment in in areas such as 3nm', while metrology intensity in gate-all-around is higher. Process control versus process: 'It's too early to call how process control specifically will look like this year' - Nova taps into both. Lead times 'are still shorter than some of our peers'; with higher visibility Nova has 'more confidence in our annual performance'. Supply: 'some pressure on the supply chain', mitigated by working with a few suppliers - 'we are managing suppliers to meet demand.'

CEO Gaby Waisman on China: 'As a result of advanced nodes growth, China's share of our revenue is expected to decrease, as we've already seen last year compared to 2024.' She sees 'an increase in demand in China for packaging, with a multitude of new customer engagements around advanced packaging and high bandwidth memory'; China is 'a very competitive market'; 'We are encouraged to see some potential growth in China this year. There is some positive momentum in the business in China compared to last quarter.'

CEO Gaby Waisman on advanced packaging and hybrid bonding: 'We have good traction with advanced packaging customers across the board, top-tier customers, as well as growth in the Chinese advanced packaging realm', and 'some initial good traction and adoption in hybrid bonding, also with top-tier customers'. For the year: 'we see similar levels of growth in advanced packaging to what our peers have already mentioned.' Record integrated-metrology revenue was driven by gate-all-around and also by new customer penetration in mature nodes and advanced packaging. On X-ray: 'We believe that X-ray could play out in a very significant role' in front-end and advanced-packaging challenges; Nova's hybrid-metrology strategy draws on a broad, homegrown optical and X-ray portfolio.
